life_summary: Dallin Harris Oaks was born on August 12, 1932, in Provo, Utah. He earned his bachelor's degree in accounting from Brigham Young University in 1954 and pursued advanced legal education at the University of Chicago Law School on scholarship, graduating with a J.D. in 1957. As a law student, he served as editor-in-chief of the University of Chicago Law Review. Following law school, Oaks clerked for Chief Justice Earl Warren from 1957 to 1958, an experience that shaped his constitutional law thinking. He practiced corporate litigation at Kirkland & Ellis before joining the University of Chicago's law faculty, where he specialized in constitutional law and evidence.
church_summary: Oaks served as BYU's eighth president from 1971 to 1980, overseeing the creation of the law school and business school while promoting affirmative action policies and emphasizing the equal treatment of women in the workplace. He served on the Utah Supreme Court from 1980 to 1984 before joining the Church's Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1984. Presidents Gerald Ford and Ronald Reagan both considered him for appointment to the U.S. Supreme Court—Ford in 1975 and Reagan in 1981—though neither appointment was ultimately made. Oaks became president of the Church in October 2025 following Russell M. Nelson's death.
